concerns.text: The plan cites 'Cadenza-Labs/apollo-llama3.3-sandbagging-v2-wmdp-mmlu' and 'EC-DGT-AI/EU-MMLU' as sources for the 'Training subset for synthetic generation context' and 'Additional dev subset'. These are highly specific, non-standard, or potentially hallucinated dataset identifiers on Hugging Face. The primary MMLU source (TIGER-Lab/MMLU-Pro) is standard, but the secondary sources lack clear provenance in the plan. If these datasets do not exist or are not accessible, the 'held-out' and 'synthetic context' data generation will fail. The plan must verify these specific repository IDs exist and are appropriate for the intended 'held-out' evaluation, or revert to standard MMLU subsets (e.g., specific subject categories from the main MMLU repo) to ensure feasibility.

The plan states: 'The held-out set will be constructed by selecting specific subject categories from these verified sources that are not present in the synthetic training buffer.' However, the synthetic training buffer is generated from '10 task schemas (derived from MMLU categories)' (Methodology section). The plan does not explicitly define which 10 categories are used for the synthetic buffer versus which are reserved for the held-out set. Without this explicit mapping (e.g., 'Buffer: History, Geography; Held-out: Physics, Chemistry'), the 'Non-Circular Validation' (Constitution Principle VII) cannot be verified. The plan must cite the specific subject categories used for each set to ensure the held-out data is truly distinct.
